title: introduce-tool-binding-hints-and-stream-attribution-for-openai-compat
author: Priya Nambiar
description:
Motivation:
As part of improving OpenAI function/tool calling compatibility we encountered two recurring issues in customer integrations: 1) ambiguity about which service produced a given streaming fragment when responses included interleaved assistant messages and tool invocation frames, and 2) loss of schema mapping metadata when the compatibility layer translated between native Redwood tool signatures and OpenAI-style function schemas.

Summary of changes:
- Add an optional Tool-Binding hint header (X-Redwood-Tool-Binding) emitted by the compatibility adapter when mapping a bound Redwood tool to an OpenAI function schema. This header carries a compact binding id and version (e.g. tb:search.v2) to be threaded through streaming fragments for attribution and debugging.
- Extend streaming envelope fragments with an attribution field in the framed protocol (compat-only): a lightweight "source" token ("assistant", "tool:<binding>", "system") added as a top-level framing tag so fragments can be disambiguated by downstream consumers without changing payload bodies.
- Preserve schema provenance: when the adapter synthesizes an OpenAI function schema from an annotated Redwood tool definition, we now inject a provenance comment block into the schema description (machine-parseable key/value pairs) so roundtrip tooling can rehydrate original binding metadata.
- Update the OpenAI-compat adapter to prefer explicit binding ids for tool_choice resolution. When multiple tools match, the adapter uses binding hints + deterministic score tiebreak instead of random selection.
- Add end-to-end tests that assert streaming fragment ordering, attribution tags, and schema provenance extraction; add a new conformance test that replays a recorded multi-tool dialog and verifies identical events after round-trip through the adapter.

Design notes and rationale:
We intentionally kept changes compatibility-friendly: all runtime changes are behind the compatibility adapter flag (openai_compat: { tool_binding_hints: true }) and default to off for existing customers. The attribution tag is a framing-level hint (not injected into user-visible assistant content) so downstream clients that depend on exact assistant text are unaffected. The tool-binding header is optional and can be omitted in environments where headers are stripped (e.g., some proxies). The provenance comment in the function schema uses a compact JSON snippet embedded in the description field to survive systems that only persist the function schema text.

Rollout and migration:
- Feature gate: openai_compat.tool_binding_hints (off by default).
- Canary plan: enabled for two internal customers and redwood-qa for one week, monitor deltas in streaming fragment counts and compatibility tests.
- Fallback: if downstream consumers observe malformed fragments we will revert the adapter toggle and publish a hotfix to remove the framing tag.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests for the binding id generator and schema provenance serializer.
- Integration tests that run the adapter in both streaming and non-streaming modes and assert no text delta in assistant outputs.
- New e2e conformance replay test recorded as fixtures in tests/fixtures/openai-binding-replay.json.
- CI: build -> unit -> integration -> e2e conformance. All checks green on merge.

Security and privacy:
The binding id is non-sensitive and deterministic; it encodes repo-local tool name and semantic version only. We explicitly do not leak backend credentials or internal routing topology. The provenance block is limited in length and sanitized to remove developer comments.

Related work and alternatives considered:
- Embedding binding ids inline into assistant messages was rejected because it modifies user-visible content.
- Serializing provenance to a separate event stream was considered but increases operational complexity for clients that only subscribe to the primary message stream.

Notes for SDK authors and integrators:
- SDK updates for Python/TS include helpers to read fragment attribution and re-associate tool frames; documented in docs/openai-compat/tool-bindings.md.
- The adapters expose a compatibility-only header mapping table so customers can map existing function names to canonical binding ids.

Action items post-merge:
- Publish release note summarizing opt-in nature and how to enable the gate for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Add a sample in redwood-examples demonstrating multi-tool streaming playback and attribution UI.
